summary: Wang Yao (1928–2015) was a Tibetologist who studied under the traditional teacher Gongkar Tulku and later taught Qingying Chen. He served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.

Wannaporn Rienjang is a historian and archaeologist working in Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Cambridge and held posts at the British Museum, the University of Oxford (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).

Warren Crawford Cowgill (1929–1985) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and completed his PhD at Yale University (~1952–1957), where he became a professor of linguistics in 1956.

Warren Lee Todd works in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD at Lancaster University under doctoral supervisor Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad, and also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Peter Harvey, and the traditional teacher Chogye Trichen Rinpoche.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2007). His studies were supervised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, alongside teachers Phra Sudhivorayan and Somjin Sammāpañño.

Wasō Harada works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Ryukoku University and Koyasan University (MA 1984), later holding posts at Koyasan University (attested 1992), Ryukoku University (attested 1999–2006), and Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2002–2007).
Watari Yanai (1875–1926) was a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1898 to 1901 and later held a post there from ~1919 to 1926.

Wataru Ryose is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1987 under the doctoral supervision of Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances Wilson.

Wayne Chandira is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University, studying under doctoral supervisor Mark Rowe.

Wayne Proudfoot (1939–) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Harvard Divinity School and Harvard University (MTh ~1966–1969, PhD ~1969–1972), later teaching at Fordham University (~1970–1972) and Columbia University (~1972).

Wei Lin works in sinology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State University (PhD attested 2007), she has held appointments at Nanjing Municipal Museum, Western Michigan University, University of Michigan, and Transylvania University.

Wei Wu (1949–) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies who founded the International Buddhist College. Attested in 2026, he serves as Associate Professor and Director of Undergraduate Studies at Emory University.

Wei-Cheng Lin is a scholar of history, archaeology, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill until 2015, when he joined the faculty at the University of Chicago.

Wei-jen Teng works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. Educated at the University of Chicago and Harvard University (PhD attested 2011), he has held posts at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts and Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies.

Wei-ming Tu (1940–) is a philosopher and sinologist. He studied at Tunghai University and Harvard (PhD ~1962–1968), and held positions at Princeton, UC Berkeley, the East-West Center, Harvard-Yenching Institute (1996–2008), Harvard University (1999–2010), and Peking University (~2010).

Weijue Shi (1928–2016) was a Buddhist studies figure who was ordained under Linyuan in 1963 and studied under Lingyuan (~1963–1970). He founded Lin Quan Temple (1987), Chung Tai Shan, and the Chung Tai Buddhist Institute (1993).

Weirong Shen (1962–) is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He has taught Penghao Sun and held academic appointments at Renmin University of China (~2006–2020) and the University of Hong Kong.
Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University, where studies were supervised by Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

Weizhong Huang (1969–) is a scholar in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. He held a post at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2012) and serves as a professor at Renmin University of China (attested 2026).

Weldon South Coblin (1944–) is a scholar of sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics. He studied under Fang-Kuei Li (~1967–1972) and served as Professor Emeritus of Chinese at the University of Iowa, where he worked from ~1973 to 2013.
